The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 1.05 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

The judge's explanation, as written

Rider and driver: the record shows a real but small route deviation, and the fare charged on this trip is SGD 1.05 more than the policy allows. That amount is refunded to the rider; the rest of the charge stands and no separate payment is due to the driver. WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The GPS trace for TRP-02844 (EV-GPS-02844, weight 1.0) records 4.04 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off, against a platform optimal of 3.20 km (EV-TRIP-02844, weight 1.0). The excess is 0.84 km, or 26.25% of the optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both establishment tests and both pass (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I used the trace figure because POL-RD-01 makes it govern: the trip record's rounded 4.00 km would give exactly 0.80 km and fail the strict absolute gate, and the clause forbids citing it for this test. The excess is below both materiality gates (50%, 8.0 km), so the deviation is ordinary, not material: POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. I ran the profile check anyway, as the clause directs where the evidence is finely balanced: 1 deviation flag over 247 completed trips in 90 days is a ratio of about 0.004 against the 0.05 test, and 1 flag against the 3-flag test, so no repeat pattern is established on either limb. No profile field was used as a fact about this trip (POL-GEN-01). THE TRACE IS CLEAN. 46 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval over 30 seconds, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). The deviation may rest on the trace alone and no independent corroboration is needed under POL-RD-07(ii). THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's account ('One-way streets') asserts an outside traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 tests such an assertion against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. There is no advisory on file: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the 0.84 km excess nor supplies an adjusted optimal route. The assertion is discarded and I record that no advisory was on file. WHY THIS IS NOT ESCALATED. The driver asks for escalation under POL-RD-10(5) and POL-RD-13(1). I do not escalate. POL-RD-13(1) applies only where the asserting party names an evidence ID for an advisory; the driver's own account names none, and an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one. The briefs' references to the minted advisory identifier describe the gap in the bundle rather than a record the driver pointed to as its evidence; the absence of an artifact cited as nothing more than an absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not engaged, no other mandatory trigger in POL-RD-10 (1)-(8) fires, and the case is decided on the record. For both parties' information: the missing advisory is the only record that could have changed this outcome, by exonerating the route under POL-RD-03 had it existed. NO OTHER EXONERATION. No rider-requested detour: the chat log EV-CHAT-02844 is complete and holds 0 messages, so there is no instruction and no waypoint_hint to test (POL-RD-04 unavailable). No endpoint change: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no substitute figure may be derived. No pooling: the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline remains the booked optimal of 3.20 km. THE REFUND. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 (not POL-RD-11) governs and the arithmetic is not discretionary. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 3.20 km + 0.28 x 6.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 8.68. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-02844, the only artifact that carries that field. charged_total = 9.70. Refund = 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and about 10.5% of the charged total, far below the 90% share that would convert this to a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05. NO ADDITIONAL PASS-THROUGH OR BILLING CORRECTION. erp_gantries is empty, tolls and airport surcharge are 0.00, the waiting-time fee is 0.00 and the promo discount is 0.00, so there is no unmatched or phantom line for POL-RD-09(4) to refund and no off-route ERP to itemise; and under POL-RD-09(1) any such ERP would already be comprehended in the figure above and could never be stacked on it. No billing-integrity referral arises. NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. The driver was billed for 4.00 km against a 4.04 km trace, a shortfall of 0.04 km, far below the 1.0 km that POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires, so driver_compensation_sgd is null. CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. The evidence carrying this ruling - GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown - is all at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect (SGD 1.05) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue under POL-GEN-05. This ruling was made without human review and is provisional; either party may ask for a human decision, or appeal it under POL-GEN-04, within 30 days. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The measured route exceeds the booked optimal by more than the policy's absolute gate, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01. The gps_trace records 4.04 km driven against a platform optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of 0.84 km, which is 26.25% of the optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 0.84 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 26.25% is greater than the 20% proportional threshold. Neither the 50% nor the 8.0 km materiality gate is met, so the finding is an ordinary established deviation, not a material one.

evidence EV-GPS-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The governing distance figure is the trace figure, and on this trip the choice of field is decisive rather than cosmetic. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs, and it forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy for the threshold test. trip_record.actual_distance_km is 4.0 km, which yields an excess of exactly 0.80 km and FAILS the strict 'greater than 0.8 km' gate; the trace figure of 4.04 km yields 0.84 km and passes it. The unrounded trace distance is therefore what carries this claim, and the rounded convenience copy cannot be used to defeat it.

evidence EV-GPS-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The gps_trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so this deviation may rest on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration. The trace carries 46 fixes at a 10.0 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage, an empty gap list and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds between consecutive fixes. There is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The rider has therefore satisfied the POL-RD-08(b) requirement that the excess be measured from an unimpaired trace.

evidence EV-GPS-02844 · clauses POL-RD-07, POL-RD-08

kept The rider carries and has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): the trip identifier TRP-02844 matches across the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and the trace window (11:36:04 to 11:43:34) sits inside the trip_record's own started_at and ended_at. Limb (b): an excess of 0.84 km, 26.25% of optimal, measured from a trace that is unimpaired under POL-RD-07. The rider's own profile does not engage the extra-corroboration proviso in POL-RD-08, because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4 that proviso names; no profile field is relied on here as a ground of decision beyond that proviso, in accordance with POL-GEN-01.

evidence EV-TRIP-02844, EV-GPS-02844, EV-FARE-02844, EV-RPROF-02844 · clauses POL-RD-08, POL-GEN-01

kept The driver's explanation on file - 'One-way streets' - is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 requires that it be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. There is no advisory to test it against: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has an admissibility weight_multiplier of 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and the detail that no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. The artifact is impaired to zero weight and I disclose that in this claim. Because POL-RD-03's advisory comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver named no advisory evidence identifier, so the absence is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact. The consequence is that the deviation stands at the measured figure and the recomputation runs against the booked optimal route.

evidence EV-ADVIS-02844-01, EV-GPS-02844 · clauses POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08

kept No rider-requested detour exoneration is available on this record, because there is no chat content at all. The chat log for this trip is COMPLETE and holds 0 messages, with no first or last message timestamp; the trip_record likewise records chat_message_count of 0. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction from the rider, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within 3 minutes of it, and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of a waypoint_hint. No such instruction exists in this bundle, and no waypoint_hint exists to test. The clause is simply unavailable to the driver, and no distance is excluded from the excess on that footing.

evidence EV-CHAT-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-04

kept The baseline for the threshold test is the booked optimal route of 3.2 km, and no clause adjusts it. POL-RD-05 does not run: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so there was no relocation of either endpoint and no amended re-quote to re-apply. POL-RD-12 does not run: the vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline for pooled trips is irrelevant and solo_optimal_distance_km is null in any event. The 0.84 km excess therefore stands against the booked optimal of 3.2 km.

evidence EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-05, POL-RD-12

kept The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and is not discretionary. The fare_model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 (not POL-RD-11) governs, and the recomputation is: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP and tolls on the optimal route + 0 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting_time_fee - 0.00 promo_discount = 7.88 + 0.80 = 8.68. The charged_total is 9.70, so the refund is 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as the final payable figure, giving SGD 1.05. The refund is not below the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so POL-RD-02's NO_ACTION escape does not apply, and at 1.05 of 9.70 it is about 10.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that would convert the outcome into a FULL_REFUND. The surge multiplier of 1.0 was read from the fare_breakdown, which is the field POL-RD-02 names for it.

evidence EV-FARE-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-11

kept This is a rider-filed dispute and the charge is live, so the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is a refund rather than NO_ACTION. The fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the dispute was filed by the RIDER. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative: on this record it would leave the 9.70 charge standing exactly as it is, with nothing returned. A PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05 is therefore the remedy that favours the rider. I do not ask for the full SGD 2.00 contested: POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary, and SGD 1.05 is what the clause's own computation supports on this evidence.

evidence EV-FARE-02844 · clauses POL-GEN-03, POL-RD-02

kept The monetary effect of the ruling the rider seeks is small and below the automatic-execution threshold. A refund of SGD 1.05 does not exceed the execution_threshold_sgd of 8.00, so under POL-GEN-05 the amount is executed on issue rather than held in the human queue. Nothing in this case engages the mandatory escalation triggers: the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, no artifact's timestamps run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes, no exculpatory clause has been invoked against an artifact that is missing or lacks the field it requires, and the computed refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total.

evidence EV-FARE-02844, EV-TRIP-02844, EV-GPS-02844 · clauses POL-GEN-05, POL-RD-10

The driver advocate

kept The deviation gate is crossed on this trip, but only on the trace, and only narrowly. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 4.04 km against the stored optimal of 3.20 km, an excess of 0.84 km and 26.25%, so both POL-RD-01 tests pass and the driver does not contest establishment. The trace figure governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km (4.00 km, which would give exactly 0.80 km of excess and fail the absolute 'greater than 0.8 km' gate) may not be cited for the threshold test. The margin over the absolute gate is roughly 40 metres and the margin over the percentage gate is 6.25 points: this is a threshold-crossing deviation, not a material one, and the remedy must be measured accordingly.

evidence EV-GPS-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-01

evidence EV-GPS-02844, EV-DPROF-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-01, POL-RD-06

evidence EV-FARE-02844, EV-TRIP-02844 · clauses POL-RD-09, POL-RD-02

kept The driver's explanation for the longer route — the one-way street network, recorded as the counterparty statement — is on file and cannot be tested on this record. Each draft's own explanation

Rider and driver: the record shows a real but small route deviation, and the fare charged on this trip is SGD 1.05 more than the policy allows. That amount is refunded to the rider; the rest of the charge stands and no separate payment is due to the driver. WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The GPS trace for TRP-02844 (EV-GPS-02844, weight 1.0) records 4.04 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off, against a platform optimal of 3.20 km (EV-TRIP-02844, weight 1.0). The excess is 0.84 km, or 26.25% of the optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both establishment tests and both pass (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I used the trace figure because POL-RD-01 makes it govern: the trip record's rounded 4.00 km would give exactly 0.80 km and fail the strict absolute gate, and the clause forbids citing it for this test. The excess is below both materiality gates (50%, 8.0 km), so the deviation is ordinary, not material: POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. I ran the profile check anyway, as the clause directs where the evidence is finely balanced: 1 deviation flag over 247 completed trips in 90 days is a ratio of about 0.004 against the 0.05 test, and 1 flag against the 3-flag test, so no repeat pattern is established on either limb. No profile field was used as a fact about this trip (POL-GEN-01). THE TRACE IS CLEAN. 46 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval over 30 seconds, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c). The deviation may rest on the trace alone and no independent corroboration is needed under POL-RD-07(ii). THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's account ('One-way streets') asserts an outside traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 tests such an assertion against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. There is no advisory on file: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the 0.84 km excess nor supplies an adjusted optimal route. The assertion is discarded and I record that no advisory was on file. WHY THIS IS NOT ESCALATED. The driver asks for escalation under POL-RD-10(5) and POL-RD-13(1). I do not escalate. POL-RD-13(1) applies only where the asserting party names an evidence ID for an advisory; the driver's own account names none, and an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one. The briefs' references to the minted advisory identifier describe the gap in the bundle rather than a record the driver pointed to as its evidence; the absence of an artifact cited as nothing more than an absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. POL-RD-10(5) is therefore not engaged, no other mandatory trigger in POL-RD-10 (1)-(8) fires, and the case is decided on the record. For both parties' information: the missing advisory is the only record that could have changed this outcome, by exonerating the route under POL-RD-03 had it existed. NO OTHER EXONERATION. No rider-requested detour: the chat log EV-CHAT-02844 is complete and holds 0 messages, so there is no instruction and no waypoint_hint to test (POL-RD-04 unavailable). No endpoint change: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no substitute figure may be derived. No pooling: the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline remains the booked optimal of 3.20 km. THE REFUND. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 (not POL-RD-11) governs and the arithmetic is not discretionary. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 3.20 km + 0.28 x 6.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 8.68. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-02844, the only artifact that carries that field. charged_total = 9.70. Refund = 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and about 10.5% of the charged total, far below the 90% share that would convert this to a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05. NO ADDITIONAL PASS-THROUGH OR BILLING CORRECTION. erp_gantries is empty, tolls and airport surcharge are 0.00, the waiting-time fee is 0.00 and the promo discount is 0.00, so there is no unmatched or phantom line for POL-RD-09(4) to refund and no off-route ERP to itemise; and under POL-RD-09(1) any such ERP would already be comprehended in the figure above and could never be stacked on it. No billing-integrity referral arises. NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. The driver was billed for 4.00 km against a 4.04 km trace, a shortfall of 0.04 km, far below the 1.0 km that POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires, so driver_compensation_sgd is null. CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. The evidence carrying this ruling - GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown - is all at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect (SGD 1.05) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue under POL-GEN-05. This ruling was made without human review and is provisional; either party may ask for a human decision, or appeal it under POL-GEN-04, within 30 days.
This was a real but ordinary route deviation, and the refund is set by the fare arithmetic rather than by anything either side argued. THE DEVIATION. The booked optimal route was 3.2 km (EV-TRIP-02844). POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing distance figure, and EV-GPS-02844 records 4.04 km — an excess of 0.84 km, or 26.25% of optimal. Both establishment tests are met (more than the 0.8 km absolute gate and more than the 20% proportional gate), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01. The trip record's rounded 4.0 km figure may not be used for this test: on it the excess would be exactly 0.80 km and would fail the strict 'greater than 0.8 km' gate, so the unrounded 4.04 km trace figure is what carries the finding. Neither materiality gate is met (not over 50%, not over 8.0 km), so the deviation is not MATERIAL and POL-RD-06 is not engaged — no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 46 fixes, a steady 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so this excess stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration. No rider-requested detour (the chat log, EV-CHAT-02844, holds 0 messages), no endpoint amendment and no pooled itinerary bears on the baseline either. THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's stated reason for the longer route — 'One-way streets' — cannot be weighed. An external traffic cause is tested against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else, and there is none: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING, has no payload, carries weight 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It does not reduce the excess and supplies no amended optimal. WHY THIS IS NOT ESCALATED. The driver's advocate asked for escalation under POL-RD-10(5), and POL-RD-13(1) answers that request: the driver himself named no advisory identifier, and the missing artifact's identifier was minted only so that its absence itself could be pointed to. An assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so an absent advisory that no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not the contradiction POL-RD-10(5) describes; the deviation stands at the measured figure and the recomputation runs against the booked optimal. No other escalation trigger fires: the trip identifier TRP-02844 matches across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the trace is clean, no timestamps run backwards or disagree by more than 10 minutes, and the refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total. THE REFUND. The fare was METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs (not POL-RD-11, whose upfront-quote route does not apply). The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from the fare breakdown, which is the artifact POL-RD-02 names for that field. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP and tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo discount = 8.68. charged_total = 9.70. Refund = 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as the final payable figure, giving SGD 1.05. That is about 10.5% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to a full refund, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. Nothing is added on top: no gantry was crossed, no toll, airport surcharge or waiting fee was billed, so POL-RD-09 has no pass-through or billing-integrity line to correct, and under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already be comprehended here and could never be stacked. The driver is not owed compensation: the billed distance (4.0 km) falls short of the trace (4.04 km) by only 0.04 km, well under the 1.0 km POL-RD-04 threshold, and on this recorded fare the meter tracks the same trace. EXECUTION. The monetary effect, SGD 1.05, does not exceed the execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it is executed on issue. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal it once within 30 days through the platform's help channel.

The excess is below both materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%), so this is an ordinary established deviation, not a material one; the POL-RD-06 profile check and its conduct referral are not engaged, and in any event the driver profile shows 1 deviation flag in 247 completed trips, below both the 3-flag count and the 0.05 ratio. Trace integrity and burden. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 46 fixes, a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gap list and a 0.0-second maximum gap. POL-RD-07's consequences do not apply, and the rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the trace alone — trip identifier TRP-02844 matches across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the trace window sits inside the trip record's started_at/ended_at. The rider profile does not engage POL-RD-08's extra-corroboration proviso (deviation_claims_60d is 0), and no profile field has been used as a ground of decision beyond the counters the clauses name (POL-GEN-01). The driver's explanation, and the escalation argument. The driver's statement 'One-way streets' asserts an external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 requires it to be tested against the trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. There is none: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING, payload null, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The argument that this escalates the case under POL-RD-10(5) is rejected: POL-RD-13(1) provides that where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory — as here, the driver's own statement cites nothing — the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The consequence under POL-RD-13(2) is that the deviation stands at the measured figure. For the record: the driver's traffic assertion is discarded, and no advisory was on file for this trip window. Refund = 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 1.05. To both parties. This was a short metered RydeX trip on 26 August 2026: 4.04 km actually driven, billed at SGD 9.70 against a booked optimal route of 3.20 km. Everything below is read off the trip record (EV-TRIP-02844), the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02844) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02844), all of which are complete and carry full weight (1.0). Rider — your claim is partly upheld. The governing distance is the trace figure, as POL-RD-01 requires: it records 4.04 km against the 3.20 km optimal, an excess of 0.84 km, which is 26.25% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (0.84 km > 0.8 km; 26.25% > 20%), and neither materiality gate is met (0.84 km is not > 8.0 km and 26.25% is not > 50%), so this is an ordinary established deviation, not a material one. The rounded trip-record copy (4.00 km) would give exactly 0.80 km and fail the strict absolute gate; POL-RD-01 forbids citing it for the threshold test. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 46 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s. No clause adjusts the 3.20 km baseline — there are no amendments to pickup or dropoff (POL-RD-05 does not run), the vehicle type is RYDE_X not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12 does not run), and the chat log (EV-CHAT-02844) holds 0 messages, so no rider instruction exists to attribute any excess to (POL-RD-04 does not run). The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the booked optimal route: (3.80 + 0.75 × 3.20 + 0.28 × 6.00) × 1.0 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier as that clause requires, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus 0 ERP and tolls on the optimal route, plus no fixed surcharge and no waiting fee, less no promo discount = SGD 8.68. Charged_total is SGD 9.70, so the refund is SGD 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and about 10.5% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would convert the outcome to a full refund. So the amount returned is SGD 1.05 — not the SGD 2.00 contested and not the SGD 9.70 mentioned in the claim text. Nothing is added for ERP or surcharges: no gantry was crossed, no surcharge applied, and POL-RD-09(1) would in any event forbid stacking off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The monetary effect (SGD 1.05) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue under POL-GEN-05. Driver — your explanation for the longer route, 'one-way streets', cannot be weighed. The only artifact that could test an external traffic cause is the traffic advisory for this trip, and EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is absent: payload null, admissibility status MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0, and no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, exactly as POL-RD-13 provides for this pattern: the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal, and the ruling records that the explanation was discarded and that no advisory was on file. Your advocate's request to escalate under POL-RD-10(5) is declined. POL-RD-13 settles this pattern, and the explanation asserted names no road, no closure, no queue or incident and no advisory identifier; an absence in the bundle is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and nothing in POL-RD-03 would have exonerated a one-way-street network even on a complete advisory file. For completeness on the audit trail: the claim put forward on this point was discarded by the referee because it cited the impaired advisory without naming its issue code, which POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Your remaining points are accepted. Establishment is correctly conceded; POL-RD-06 is not engaged because the deviation is not material, and the profile check fails on its own terms in any event (deviation_flags_90d = 1, below the count of 3, and 1 of 247 completed trips is about 0.4%, below the 5% ratio), so there is no conduct referral — the only fields used for that test are the two POL-GEN-01 permits. The rider's profile does not engage the POL-RD-08 extra-corroboration proviso (deviation_claims_60d = 0). No driver compensation is payable: the billed distance (4.0 km) falls short of the trace distance (4.04 km) by 0.04 km, far under the 1.0 km that POL-RD-04 requires. On weight and confidence: the only artifact below full weight is the absent advisory at 0.0, which under POL-GEN-02(3) can carry no fact and is not relied on by this ruling; the facts the ruling rests on — the trace distance, the optimal distance and the charged total — are each carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and my confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. No clause produces a referral (POL-RD-06(c), POL-RD-09(4), POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-07 are all unengaged), so the referrals list is empty. This ruling is provisional and either of you may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.
